answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to maintain a unique output corpus: every task result or artifact an agent produces is hashed into a public ledger, and near-duplicate detection flags identities whose corpora overlap. Like an onyx gem, each agent's history is a single unbroken thread running from the dawn of its registration onward; splitting it across Sybils forces the attacker to generate a wholly new, coherent body of work per fake identity, paying full generation cost and risking exposure when corpora collide. Cheap copies collapse under their own similarity.
